question: What does an orange-colored road sign generally indicate?
options: a:A school zone is ahead.,b:A railroad crossing is ahead.,c:Construction
note: Orange signs warn of construction or maintenance activities; slow down and be prepared for changed traffic patterns.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line means:
options: a:Passing on the left is permitted from either direction.,b:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken line.,c:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid line.
note: When a broken yellow line is next to a solid yellow, vehicles on the side of the broken line may pass when safe; vehicles next to the solid line may not.

question: You may cross a dashed white line:
options: a:At any time.,b:When it is safe to change lanes.,c:Only during daylight hours.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed to change lanes when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit represent?
options: a:The exact speed you must always drive to avoid a ticket.,b:Only a suggested speed to follow.,c:The maximum legal speed under ideal conditions.
note: A speed limit is the maximum legal speed for ideal conditions; you should drive slower when road, weather, or traffic conditions demand it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before making a turn?
options: a:Turn the wheel immediately without signaling.,b:Increase your speed then turn.,c:Signal your intent a few seconds before turning.
note: Activate your turn signal about three to four seconds before turning to warn other road users.

question: Which signal indicates you should slow down and proceed with caution through an intersection?
options: a:A flashing red light.,b:A solid yellow light.,c:A flashing yellow light.
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down, proceed with caution, and be ready to stop if necessary.

question: When the driver behind you signals they want to pass, what should you do?
options: a:Maintain exactly the same speed.,b:Speed up to prevent them from passing.,c:Slow down to allow space in front of your vehicle for a safe pass.
note: Slow slightly to create a gap ahead of your vehicle so the overtaking driver can pass more quickly and safely.

question: What does a steady green traffic light at an intersection mean?
options: a:Must slow down and prepare to stop.,b:May drive through the intersection if the road is clear.,c:Must stop and check for oncoming traffic before proceeding.
note: A steady green light means you may proceed through the intersection if it is clear. You may also turn, but you must yield to pedestrians and other traffic as required.

question: How should you drive in fog to reduce risk?
options: a:Reduce speed, drive cautiously, and use low-beam headlights.,b:Use high beams to see farther.,c:Use hazard lights only.
note: In fog, slow down, be cautious, and use low beams because high beams reflect back and reduce visibility.

question: What best ensures safety when backing a vehicle?
options: a:Check rearview mirrors only.,b:Check behind the vehicle on foot before getting in.,c:Honk immediately before reversing.
note: Because it's hard to see from the driver's seat, walk to the rear of the vehicle first to check for children or objects before backing.

question: What have studies shown about wearing a seat belt properly?
options: a:It increases the chance of fatality.,b:It reduces the risk of serious injury in a crash.,c:It reduces damage to your vehicle.
note: Properly worn seat belts significantly reduce the chances of serious injury or death in crashes.

question: Which activities can cause distracted driving?
options: a:Only adjusting the radio.,b:Eating,c:Only texting.
note: Many common tasks—eating, phone use, or adjusting audio—distract drivers and increase crash risk.

question: To help prevent fatigue on a long trip, what should you do?
options: a:Drive with one eye open at a time.,b:Do arm exercises every hour.,c:Stop and rest approximately every two hours.
note: To reduce fatigue, stop regularly—about every two hours—for a short break, rest, or stretch; if drowsy, stop driving immediately and rest.

question: Approximately how far might a fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling 55 mph take to stop?
options: a:Up to 400 feet.,b:About 50 feet.,c:About 125 feet.
note: Large, fully loaded tractor-trailers require much longer distances to stop than passenger cars—up to nearly 400 feet at 55 mph.

question: Regarding pedestrians, what is the driver's responsibility?
options: a:Only yield if the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk.,b:Do everything possible to avoid striking a pedestrian and yield the right-of-way.,c:Assume pedestrians must yield to vehicles.
note: Drivers must be alert and yield to pedestrians to prevent collisions, even if the pedestrian is not lawfully crossing.

question: What factor significantly affects your ability to stop a vehicle?
options: a:Road conditions (wet, icy, gravel),b:Signal lights ahead,c:Time of day only
note: Stopping distance is heavily influenced by road surface and condition; reduce speed accordingly when roads are poor.

question: Is it legal to cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass another vehicle?
options: a:No.,b:Yes.,c:Only if there is no oncoming traffic.
note: Two solid yellow lines mean no passing or crossing for either direction except to turn into a driveway or similar approved location.

question: How should you respond when near a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:Slow down, yield the right-of-way, and be prepared to stop.,b:Take the right-of-way because vehicles have priority.,c:Proceed normally without slowing down.
note: Slow, yield, and be ready to stop whenever you encounter a blind pedestrian using a cane or guide dog to ensure their safety.

question: What effect does alcohol have on reflexes and reaction time?
options: a:Wakes you up.,b:Puts you to sleep.,c:Slows reflexes and reaction time.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows brain activity, reducing reaction time and impairing judgment and coordination needed for safe driving.

question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, what is the safest reaction?
options: a:Flash your lights to let them know they are wrong.,b:Speed up and try to retaliate.,c:Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.
note: Avoid escalating the situation. Remain calm, give the aggressive driver space, and if necessary report the incident to authorities when safe.

question: When approaching an emergency vehicle stopped on the right with lights flashing, you should:
options: a:Maintain your current speed and drive in the right lane.,b:Reduce your speed and safely vacate the lane closest to the emergency vehicle.,c:Maintain your current speed and move quickly into a lane farther away from the emergency vehicle.
note: Slow down and move over one lane away from stopped emergency vehicles when it is safe to do so; if you cannot safely change lanes, reduce speed and proceed with caution.

question: On a narrow road with an obstructed view approaching a curve, the best action is to:
options: a:Stop the car,b:Rapidly turn your headlights on and off several times.,c:Sound your horn and stay close to the right edge of the road while proceeding carefully.
note: If visibility is blocked on a narrow mountain road, sound your horn to warn oncoming traffic and proceed slowly while staying close to the right edge.

question: If your vehicle has Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) and it starts to lose traction, what should you do?
options: a:Pump the brakes.,b:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.,c:Press and hold the gas pedal.
note: If your vehicle has ABS, press and hold the brake pedal firmly; the system will pump the brakes automatically to help you maintain control.

question: What do round traffic signs typically warn drivers about?
options: a:No passing zones.,b:School zones.,c:Railroad crossings ahead.
note: Circular signs are used for railroad crossing warnings; approach them with caution.

question: On long trips, how can you prevent drowsiness?
options: a:Turn on your car radio.,b:Slow down.,c:Stop at regular intervals to rest and stretch.
note: Schedule regular stops to rest, stretch, and refresh; do not rely solely on caffeine or music to prevent drowsiness.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How early should you signal before passing another vehicle?
options: a:Signal after you begin the lane change.,b:Signal only just before you change lanes.,c:Signal early enough for other drivers to know your plans in advance.
note: You should signal early enough so other drivers understand your intentions before you start the passing maneuver.

question: If an approaching train is near enough or going fast enough to be a danger, what must you do?
options: a:Cross the tracks at your own risk.,b:Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: If a train is close enough to be a hazard, you must not cross the tracks until the train has fully passed and it is safe.

question: If you are being tailgated and there is an open lane to your right, what should you do?
options: a:Increase your speed to put more distance between you.,b:Slow down abruptly to discourage the tailgater.,c:Move over to the right lane if it is safe to do so.
note: If a lane is available to the right, move over to let the tailgater pass; if not, slow gradually when safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you approach a flashing yellow traffic signal, how should you respond?
options: a:Come to a complete stop.,b:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light means caution — slow down and proceed carefully if it is safe to do so.

question: What color pavement markings separate lanes moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Yellow and white,b:White,c:Yellow
note: Yellow pavement markings are used to separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road, what must you be prepared to do?
options: a:Use the shoulder to pass the vehicle.,b:Flash your lights at oncoming traffic to warn them.,c:Move into the lane used by oncoming traffic to pass only when it is safe and legal.
note: Passing on a two-lane, two-way road often requires entering the oncoming lane; only pass when you can do so safely and legally.

question: If you are involved in an accident, what should you do first?
options: a:Help the injured if it is safe to do so.,b:Call the police if necessary.,c:Stop immediately at the scene.
note: Stop at the scene, render aid if you can safely do so, call emergency services and the police, and exchange information; do not leave.

question: What is the safest way to transport small children in a vehicle?
options: a:Have a strong adult hold the child in their arms.,b:Allow the child to stand in the back seat.,c:Use proper child restraint seats appropriate for the child's size and age.
note: Children must be secured in appropriate child safety seats or boosters; no adult can safely hold a child during a crash.

question: What maneuvers are allowed from a center left-turn lane marked for left turns?
options: a:You may pass slow-moving traffic.,b:You may make left turns from the lane.,c:You may make U-turns.
note: A center left-turn lane is reserved for left turns (and for completing U-turns where permitted); it is not for passing or through traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic signals are out due to a power outage, how should you proceed at an intersection?
options: a:Park and wait for power to be restored.,b:Treat the intersection as a four-way stop and yield accordingly.,c:Turn on your hazard lights and go through without stopping.
note: When signals are not functioning, drivers should yield in the same order as at a four-way stop and proceed cautiously.

question: Which item is NOT a factor in determining how far it takes to stop your vehicle?
options: a:Braking distance,b:Steering ability,c:Reaction distance
note: Stopping distance is determined by perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance; steering ability is not a direct factor in stopping distance calculation.

question: What can happen to a bicyclist who does not obey traffic laws?
options: a:Can be ticketed.,b:Will always receive a warning from law enforcement.,c:Is in the right because bicyclists don't have to obey traffic laws.
note: Bicyclists have the same responsibilities and duties as drivers; they can be cited for violations of traffic laws.

question: If you are stopped by a police officer, how should you behave?
options: a:Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.,b:Get your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.,c:Remain in your vehicle with hands visible on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach.
note: Stay in your vehicle unless instructed otherwise, keep your hands visible (on the wheel), and wait for the officer to request your documents.

question: Be alert to motorcycles because:
options: a:They are more difficult to see than cars.,b:Motorcyclists are less skilled drivers than other motorists.,c:They rarely use their headlights.
note: Motorcycles are smaller and harder to see; they can be hidden in blind spots and their speed/distance are harder to judge.

question: What does the term 'No zone' refer to?
options: a:An area where radios must be muted.,b:A special speed zone near schools.,c:Blind spots around a truck or bus where smaller vehicles disappear from view.
note: 'No zone' describes the truck or bus blind spots on various sides where the driver cannot see smaller vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red light on a traffic signal means:
options: a:The traffic signal is broken.,b:You do not have to come to a complete stop.,c:The same thing as a stop sign.
note: A flashing red light has the same meaning as a stop sign: stop completely, yield as required, and go when safe.

question: An octagonal traffic sign always indicates what?
options: a:A speed limit sign.,b:A stop sign.,c:A hospital sign.
note: The eight-sided (octagonal) sign always means STOP; come to a full stop at the limit line or before entering the crosswalk or intersection.

question: What effect does alcohol have on your driving skills and judgment?
options: a:It helps driving skills but harms your judgment.,b:It has no effect on either driving skills or judgment.,c:It harms both driving skills and judgment.
note: Alcohol impairs vision, reaction time, coordination, and judgment—functions essential for safe driving.

question: What do two solid yellow lines on the pavement indicate?
options: a:Passing is allowed for drivers from both directions.,b:Passing is allowed only at the top of hills.,c:Passing is not allowed from either direction.
note: Two solid yellow centerlines mean no passing from either direction except where turning into a driveway or similar maneuver is permitted.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you turn your wheels when parking downhill on a two-way street?
options: a:Turn your wheels to the left (away from curb).,b:Keep your wheels pointed straight ahead.,c:Turn your wheels to the right (toward the curb).
note: When parked facing downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb so if the vehicle rolls it will roll away from traffic.

question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches from behind?
options: a:Speed up to create distance between you and the emergency vehicle.,b:Slow down but remain in your lane.,c:Immediately pull to the curb or edge of the roadway and stop.
note: Upon hearing a siren or seeing flashing lights, yield the right-of-way by pulling to the nearest curb or edge and stopping until the emergency vehicle passes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does the driver's left arm extended downward signify?
options: a:The driver intends to turn left.,b:The driver intends to turn right.,c:The driver intends to stop.
note: A left arm pointed down is a hand signal indicating the driver will stop or slow; adjust your driving accordingly.

question: What minimum following distance should you maintain under normal conditions?
options: a:A two-second space cushion.,b:A three-second space cushion.,c:200 feet at all times.
note: A minimum three-second following distance is recommended; increase it for higher speeds or poor conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a \No standing\" sign mean at a location?"
options: a:You may park there if you stay in the vehicle.,b:You may never stop your vehicle there for any reason.,c:You may stop temporarily only to load or discharge passengers.
note: A No Standing zone allows only short stops to pick up or drop off passengers; parking or waiting is not permitted.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to make a right turn, your vehicle should be positioned:
options: a:Near the center of the street.,b:As far to the right side of the road as practicable.,c:Close to the left side of the road.
note: Move as far right as is safe and legal before making a right turn to avoid crossing lanes unnecessarily.

question: In foggy conditions, you should use your:
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: Use low beam headlights (and fog lights if equipped) in fog; high beams can reflect off the fog and reduce visibility.

question: When driving at night and an oncoming vehicle approaches, your headlights should be:
options: a:Should be off. Use your parking lights.,b:Should be on their low beam setting.,c:Should be on their high beam setting.
note: Use low beam headlights when approaching or following other vehicles to avoid blinding other drivers.

question: If you approach a railroad crossing and do not see or hear a train, when must you stop?
options: a:If a crossing gate is lowered.,b:If the crossing lights are flashing.,c:For stop signs, flashing lights, or lowered gates.
note: You must stop when a stop sign is posted; you must also stop for flashing lights or a lowered gate or any sign that indicates a train is approaching.

question: What actions reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Drive faster to get through wet patches quicker.,b:Use tires with improper air pressure to increase surface area.,c:Do not speed on wet roads and maintain proper tire pressure and tread.
note: Hydroplaning risk decreases with lower speeds and properly inflated, well-treaded tires; replace tires with worn tread.

question: Which practice helps conserve gasoline while driving?
options: a:Accelerating quickly.,b:Sitting in your driveway with the engine running.,c:Slowing down gradually and avoiding unnecessary braking.
note: Avoiding sudden stops and accelerating smoothly conserves fuel because frequent hard accelerations consume more gasoline.

question: Railroad crossings should always be considered:
options: a:Dangerous.,b:Safe to cross at all times.,c:Places to park temporarily.
note: Railroad crossings present a significant hazard; always look, listen, and obey signals and barriers before crossing.

question: What color are signs that indicate areas of public recreation?
options: a:Orange.,b:Red.,c:Brown.
note: Brown signs designate cultural, historical, or recreational sites and are helpful when traveling unfamiliar areas.

question: What is the safest way to pass a bicyclist?
options: a:Drive in the bicycle lane until you pass them.,b:Honk to let the bicyclist know you are passing.,c:Slow down and give the bicyclist as much space as possible.
note: When passing a bicycle, slow and give a wide berth; bicyclists have little protection and should not be crowded.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning in wet conditions?
options: a:Drive through deeper puddles rather than skirt them.,b:Increase your speed gradually.,c:Drive more slowly.
note: Hydroplaning is more likely at higher speeds; slowing down and avoiding standing water reduces the risk.

question: Why must you use increased caution while driving at night?
options: a:Traffic moves faster at night.,b:Drivers cannot see as well in the dark.,c:There is more traffic at night.
note: Reduced visibility at night makes it harder to detect hazards; headlights are required when you can't see persons/vehicles for 500 feet.

question: What do highway pavement markings and signs provide for drivers?
options: a:They are only found in construction zones.,b:They provide information and guidance for safe driving.,c:They are usually not important.
note: Pavement markings and traffic signs help drivers position vehicles, indicate passing zones, and warn about upcoming conditions—obey them.

question: What does a yellow and black diamond-shaped sign typically warn you about?
options: a:Conditions on or near the road ahead.,b:The nearest towns and distances.,c:Traffic laws and regulations you must obey.
note: Yellow diamond signs are warning signs that alert drivers to upcoming changes in road conditions or hazards.

question: How should you respond to an aggressive driver?
options: a:Retaliate by tailgating them.,b:Cut them off to make them slow down.,c:Avoid eye contact
note: Remain calm, avoid escalating the situation, and create distance between you and the aggressive driver.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which traffic signal requires you to stop at an intersection?
options: a:A steady yellow light.,b:A yellow arrow.,c:A flashing red light.
note: A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign — come to a complete stop, then proceed when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Parking or stopping on the shoulder of a freeway is allowed:
options: a:If no part of your vehicle is on the road.,b:As long as you turn on your four-way (emergency) flashers.,c:Only in case of emergency.
note: It is illegal to park on a freeway shoulder except in an emergency; using flashers does not make parking there legal unless it is an emergency.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a red traffic signal require you to do?
options: a:Proceed with caution.,b:Stop before entering the intersection,c:Slow down if comfortable.
note: A red light requires you to stop before the intersection, stop line, or crosswalk and remain stopped until it's safe to go.

question: How would you classify distracted driving?
options: a:Very uncommon.,b:Nothing to worry about.,c:Extremely risky behavior.
note: Distracted driving is highly risky and endangers everyone on the road; full attention helps prevent crashes.

question: Why is a leaky exhaust system hazardous?
options: a:It improves fuel economy.,b:It causes a loss of hearing.,c:It can lead to carbon monoxide poisoning.
note: A leaking exhaust can allow carbon monoxide to enter the passenger compartment, posing a serious poisoning risk; repair leaks promptly.

question: When driving on major highways, which habits should you maintain?
options: a:Keep your eyes moving and avoid fixed gaze.,b:All of the above.,c:Stay alert and be ready to react to hazards.
note: On major highways remain alert, keep your eyes moving to prevent highway hypnosis, and be prepared to react to sudden hazards.

question: Traffic lanes moving in the same direction are divided by ____ lines.
options: a:Yellow,b:Red,c:White
note: Solid and broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction; yellow lines separate opposite directions.

question: Which statement about driving in changing weather is true?
options: a:A sudden change in weather requires a change in driving habits.,b:You should always drive faster in rain and fog.,c:Be less aware of vehicles behind you in inclement weather.
note: Adjust driving to suit weather: slow down in rain or fog and be aware of vehicles behind you that may be moving too fast for conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following should you do when changing lanes?
options: a:Speed up suddenly and dart into the lane.,b:Signal only and rely on mirrors alone.,c:Check mirrors
note: Before changing lanes, signal, check your rearview and side mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots.

question: When meeting a car with high beams that blind you, what should you do?
options: a:Flash your lights on and off.,b:Use your high beams to return the glare.,c:Look toward the right edge of the road until it passes.
note: Avoid looking directly at the high beams; glance to the right edge of the road to maintain orientation until the vehicle passes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers may not pass from either side of which centerline marking?
options: a:Combination solid and broken yellow line.,b:Double solid yellow line.,c:Single broken yellow line.
note: A double solid yellow centerline means passing from either direction is prohibited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you are already inside an intersection and the light turns yellow, what should you do?
options: a:Continue carefully through the intersection.,b:Immediately reverse out of the intersection.,c:Stop in the center of the intersection.
note: If you are already in the intersection when a steady yellow appears, clear it carefully rather than stopping abruptly.

question: When you see a flashing yellow arrow for left turns, what does it allow you to do?
options: a:Make a protected left turn without yielding.,b:Stop and wait for a green arrow before turning.,c:Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: A flashing yellow arrow permits left turns but requires you to yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning.

question: How should you check your blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Only use your left side mirror.,b:Only use the rearview mirror.,c:Glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.
note: Quickly look over your shoulder toward the lane you plan to enter to check for vehicles hidden in your blind spot.

question: What is the best response to being tailgated?
options: a:Slam on your brakes to make them back off.,b:Speed up to increase the distance between you and them.,c:Change lanes or gradually slow to encourage them to pass.
note: If someone follows too closely, safely change lanes or reduce speed gradually to allow them to pass and reduce rear-end collision risk.

question: Drivers who eat and drink while driving:
options: a:Are better drivers because they are not hungry.,b:Make no driving errors.,c:Have trouble driving slowly.
note: Eating or drinking while driving distracts you and increases the likelihood of lane deviations and errors.

question: At a multi-track railroad crossing, after a train passes you should:
options: a:Cross immediately when the first train passes.,b:Stop on the first track and look for another train.,c:Wait until you have a clear view of all tracks before proceeding.
note: Do not start across until you can see all tracks are clear; there may be another train approaching on a parallel track.

question: If another vehicle appears likely to hit you, what is an appropriate immediate action?
options: a:Turn off your headlights to avoid startling them.,b:Sound your horn to warn the other driver.,c:Wave your arms out the window to get their attention.
note: Use your horn to alert drivers or pedestrians of imminent danger; it is an effective warning tool in emergencies.

question: If an oncoming vehicle is in your lane heading toward you, what should you do first?
options: a:Steer left into oncoming traffic to avoid the collision.,b:Accelerate straight ahead to pass it quickly.,c:Sound your horn
note: Honk to attract attention, attempt to escape to the right, and brake firmly if a collision is unavoidable — do not swerve left into oncoming traffic.

question: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) depends on all of the following EXCEPT:
options: a:How much you drink.,b:Your body weight.,c:The type of alcoholic beverage.
note: BAC is affected by the amount consumed, the time over which drinks are consumed, and body weight; the type of beverage does not determine BAC.

question: What does defensive driving primarily involve?
options: a:Getting ahead of slower drivers to prevent conflicts.,b:Anticipating dangerous situations and taking actions to avoid accidents.,c:Following the vehicle ahead at a close distance to reduce lane changes.
note: Defensive driving means identifying potential hazards early and acting to prevent collisions rather than reacting too late.

question: If your wheels slip off the edge of the road, what should you do?
options: a:Jerk the wheel and force the car back onto the pavement quickly.,b:Speed up to get back on the road.,c:Continue with wheels off the pavement and gradually return
note: If you drift off the pavement, decelerate smoothly and return to the road gradually once at a safe speed; avoid abrupt steering or braking.

question: Before backing out of your driveway when children are nearby, you should:
options: a:Sound your horn so the children will hear you.,b:Rev your engine to warn the children that you are moving.,c:Walk to the back of the car to be sure the way is clear.
note: Get out and check behind your vehicle before backing if children are near; do not rely only on mirrors or cameras.

question: Which driving technique helps avoid crashes on icy or snowy roads?
options: a:Add extra weight to your vehicle to improve traction.,b:Get off the highways as quickly as possible.,c:Reduce your speed and increase your following distance.
note: Lower speeds and greater following distances give you more time to react and reduce the chance of skids or collisions in icy or snowy conditions.

question: Why should you be especially careful when passing a bicyclist?
options: a:The cyclist may swerve to avoid an object, creating a hazard.,b:The bicycle always has the right-of-way.,c:You are moving faster than the bicycle so you don't need to be cautious.
note: Bicyclists may need to swerve to avoid potholes, debris, or other hazards. Give them space and pass only when it is safe to do so.

question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians?
options: a:Only when the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver.,b:Always when the pedestrian is in the street,c:Only when the pedestrian uses a crosswalk.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the roadway; avoid hitting them even if they are not using a crosswalk or are otherwise careless.

question: What is the effect of taking drugs together with alcohol?
options: a:It has no added risk beyond alcohol alone.,b:It increases the risk of causing a crash.,c:It reduces alcohol's effects on driving ability.
note: Combining alcohol with prescription, OTC, or illegal drugs can increase impairment and the risk of a crash.

question: Which statement about winter driving is not true?
options: a:Using cruise control in winter weather is a safe thing to do.,b:Checking your vehicle's antifreeze and windshield washer fluid levels is especially important during the winter.,c:Winter is the most difficult driving season.
note: You should not use cruise control in snow or icy conditions; winter driving requires extra precautions like checking fluids and using appropriate tires.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a turn, what should you do with your speed?
options: a:Maintain your current speed.,b:Increase your speed to clear the intersection faster.,c:Reduce your speed so you can maintain control.
note: When turning you should slow to a speed that lets you remain in your lane and maintain control to react to unexpected events.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended upward, what does that signal mean?
options: a:The driver plans to turn left.,b:The driver is planning to stop.,c:The driver plans to turn right.
note: A left-arm raised upward is the hand signal for a right turn; interpret this when following slower vehicles or cyclists using hand signals.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, if two drivers arrive at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the left.,b:The larger vehicle,c:The driver on the right.
note: At simultaneous arrivals at a four-way stop, yield to the vehicle on your right; proceed when it is safe.

question: If an approaching vehicle fails to dim its high beams, where should you look?
options: a:Toward the right side of the road to avoid glare.,b:Directly at the center of the road.,c:Toward the left side of the road.
note: Glancing to the right edge of the road reduces glare and helps you maintain your lane until the vehicle passes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is correct about turning at a steady red light?
options: a:You may make a U-turn anywhere unless a sign forbids it.,b:You may turn left into any lane on a multilane road as long as no cars are in your way.,c:You may turn right after stopping and yielding to cross traffic unless otherwise posted.
note: At a steady red, you may turn right after coming to a complete stop and yielding to pedestrians and cross traffic unless a sign prohibits it. (Left turns on red are allowed only from one-way onto one-way where posted.)

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn, what must you do regarding other road users?
options: a:Expect pedestrians to yield to you.,b:Yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians unless signaled otherwise.,c:Proceed quickly because you have the right-of-way.
note: Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians when making left turns, and follow traffic control devices or officers' directions.

question: If you begin to feel tired while driving, the best action is to:
options: a:Get some coffee.,b:Stop driving and rest.,c:Open your window and continue driving.
note: Drowsy driving is dangerous; stop driving and rest or find accommodations rather than attempting to continue while tired.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach an intersection with a flashing yellow light, what is the correct action?
options: a:Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.,b:Stop and wait for the light to change.,c:Drive carefully through the intersection after slowing and scanning for hazards.
note: A flashing yellow requires you to slow and be prepared to yield; proceed only when it is safe to do so.

question: Under what circumstances may you drive around lowered railroad crossing gates?
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:When the train has passed.,c:When the lights have stopped flashing.
note: Never go around lowered gates; wait until gates are fully raised and signals have stopped before crossing.

question: How should you reduce the effects of oncoming headlight glare at night?
options: a:Turn on your interior lights to reduce glare.,b:Look straight ahead at the oncoming headlights.,c:Look toward the right side of the road ahead and avoid staring at the lights.
note: If oncoming drivers fail to dim their lights, look toward the right edge of the roadway to reduce glare and preserve your night vision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you make room for vehicles merging onto a freeway?
options: a:Safely merge out of the right lane to allow them access.,b:Always drive in the far left lane.,c:Abruptly slow to let them in.
note: When another vehicle is entering from a ramp, if it is safe, change lanes to allow a smoother merge; avoid abrupt braking.

question: When parking parallel to a curb, you must park within:
options: a:Park within 18 inches of the curb or edge of the roadway.,b:Park facing oncoming traffic.,c:Park within 24 inches of the curb or edge of the roadway.
note: Park parallel and within 18 inches of the curb or edge of the roadway, facing the same direction as traffic on that side of the street.

question: A person using a white cane or guide dog is most likely:
options: a:Deaf.,b:Part of a traffic study.,c:A blind pedestrian.
note: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians who are blind and using a white cane or guide dog.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which has priority over signs, signals, and pavement markings?
options: a:A stop sign.,b:A steady red light.,c:A police officer directing traffic.
note: A traffic officer's directions override traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings; always obey a person authorized to direct traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A pedestrian begins to cross in front of your vehicle. You should:
options: a:Flash your lights.,b:Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop.
note: Always yield to pedestrians in crosswalks. Slow down and stop if necessary to allow the pedestrian to cross safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection where you need to turn but are in the wrong lane, what should you do?
options: a:Drive to the next intersection and turn from the correct lane.,b:Turn from your current lane after signaling.,c:Cut across traffic quickly to make the turn.
note: Do not make last-minute lane changes; go to the next intersection and turn from the proper lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you turn onto a street that has multiple lanes traveling in your direction, where should you end up?
options: a:In the middle lane.,b:In the lane closest to the lane you were in before the turn.,c:In any lane you choose after turning.
note: When turning onto a multi-lane road, enter the lane closest to your original lane and do not change lanes while completing the turn.

question: What should you remember when driving on wet pavement?
options: a:Wet roads do not cause hydroplaning.,b:Pavement can be especially slippery right after rain begins.,c:You should always follow the posted speed limit regardless of conditions.
note: Road surfaces are most slick shortly after rainfall begins due to oils on the pavement; slow down and increase following distance.

question: When you hear or see an approaching emergency vehicle, you should:
options: a:Proceed slowly and let it pass in traffic.,b:Stop immediately in your current lane.,c:Drive as far right as safely possible and stop.
note: On two-lane or undivided roads, pull to the right and stop, avoiding stopping in an intersection, to allow emergency vehicles to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving in Idaho, what speed principle must you follow?
options: a:Always drive 10 mph below the posted limit.,b:Drive at a speed that is reasonable and prudent for conditions.,c:Always drive at the posted maximum speed.
note: You must drive at a speed that is safe for current road, weather, and traffic conditions even if it is below the posted limit.

question: What does a double solid yellow line down the center of a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers may pass if safe.,b:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.,c:Traffic is moving in opposite directions and passing is prohibited.
note: Double solid yellow center lines separate opposing traffic and indicate that passing is not allowed for vehicles in either direction.

question: How does smoking or preparing to smoke while driving affect your safety?
options: a:It has no effect on driving abilities.,b:It helps maintain driver alertness.,c:It is a distracting activity that can reduce driving performance.
note: Smoking while driving requires hand and visual attention away from driving, creating distractions that increase crash risk.

question: What should a driver do upon seeing an animal on the roadway?
options: a:Pass the animal slowly and cautiously to avoid startling it.,b:Pass closely to minimize delay.,c:Ignore it and maintain speed.
note: Exercise caution and pass slowly to avoid frightening the animal and creating a hazard.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a flashing red traffic light, drivers should:
options: a:Come to a complete stop and then proceed when safe.,b:Stop if a police officer is nearby.,c:Drive through the intersection if there is no crossing traffic.
note: A flashing red light means stop; treat it like a stop sign: stop, yield, and proceed when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a crowded freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Yield to traffic already on the freeway.,b:Use your side and rearview mirrors and check your blind spots.,c:Use the acceleration lane to match speed to freeway traffic.
note: Use the entrance ramp to accelerate and match the flow of traffic, check mirrors and blind spots, and yield to vehicles already on the freeway before merging.

question: When approaching a stopped school bus displaying its stop arm and flashing lights, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and pass carefully if no children are visible.,b:Honk before passing on the left.,c:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped until the stop arm is withdrawn.
note: Drivers must stop for stopped school buses using stop signals and may not proceed until the bus indicates it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which rule is a good guideline to remember about passing?
options: a:Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only as needed.,b:Pass on the right whenever possible.,c:Try to get to the front of slow-moving traffic to see better.
note: Passing increases collision risk. Drive with the flow of traffic within the speed limit and pass only when necessary and safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must yield to other drivers under which circumstance listed?
options: a:Only where a yield sign is present.,b:Only when you want to yield.,c:When workers are present in construction zones.
note: Yield to vehicles and pedestrians in highway construction areas and drive with extra caution whenever workers are present.

question: At a light rail intersection you should always:
options: a:Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.,b:Look both ways before crossing tracks.,c:Pay attention and obey all traffic signals.
note: Never go around lowered gates; always obey crossing signals and signs and look both ways before turning across light rail tracks.

question: If you are in a line of traffic crossing tracks with no gates or signals, what should you ensure before entering?
options: a:You may pass slower drivers while on the tracks.,b:You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.,c:There is room for your vehicle to get all the way across the tracks without stopping.
note: Make sure you can clear the tracks completely before proceeding; never stop on the rails and never pass other vehicles while crossing.

question: When a traffic signal shows a steady green arrow, what are drivers allowed to do?
options: a:Merge into the lane indicated without yielding.,b:Turn in the direction of the arrow after yielding to vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection.,c:Stop and wait for a circular green.
note: A green arrow allows turning in the arrow's direction, but you must yield to traffic and pedestrians already present in the intersection.

question: If someone is injured in an accident you are involved in, what should you do?
options: a:Move the injured away from the scene immediately.,b:Always leave the injured where they are.,c:Not move the injured unnecessarily; keep them warm and provide first aid if trained.
note: Do not move injured persons unless absolutely necessary; keep them warm and provide basic first aid and call for professional help.

question: When approaching an accident scene, what should you do?
options: a:Stop in the roadway to view the accident.,b:Drive to the scene and get out to take photos.,c:Stop only if you are involved or if emergency help has not yet arrived; otherwise keep moving and stay alert.
note: Do not stop just to look; only stop if you are directly involved or if emergency responders have not yet arrived and you can safely help.

question: What do working brake lights communicate to drivers behind you?
options: a:You are about to turn.,b:You have your emergency brake on.,c:You are slowing down or stopping.
note: Brake lights signal to drivers behind you that you are reducing speed or stopping; they must be maintained in working order.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle using its lights, you must:
options: a:Slow down and keep moving in your lane.,b:Keep driving in your lane.,c:Pull to the right curb and stop.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights or siren, immediately pull over to the curb or side of the road and stop to allow it to pass.

question: If you stop along the road at night, what lights should you use?
options: a:Turn on emergency flashers and keep low-beam headlights on.,b:Turn off all lights.,c:Use only parking lights.
note: At night, leave low beams on and use hazard flashers so other road users can see your stopped vehicle.

question: When driving on an interstate, what must you do before changing lanes?
options: a:Always use cruise control.,b:Signal,c:Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.
note: Before changing lanes on an interstate, signal and check mirrors and blind spots; do not stop on the shoulder unless an emergency occurs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you meet an oncoming vehicle on a narrow road, what should you do?
options: a:Pull completely off the road and stop.,b:Allow the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road.,c:Demand the other vehicle pull over to make room.
note: On narrow roads you must give oncoming traffic at least one-half of the main-traveled portion so both vehicles have adequate space to pass safely.

question: Double solid yellow lines down the middle of the road mean:
options: a:Pedestrian crossing ahead.,b:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,c:Railroad crossing ahead.
note: Double solid yellow lines indicate no passing from either direction; only cross them for permitted left turns or as otherwise allowed by law.

question: If there are two railroad tracks side by side, when one train clears you should:
options: a:Proceed immediately after one train passes.,b:Look for another train on the other track before crossing.,c:Always stop before crossing.
note: After one train passes, check for other trains on adjacent tracks before crossing; never assume it's safe immediately.

question: Which of the following is a common sign of a drunk driver?
options: a:They are making quick and sudden stops.,b:They are weaving between lanes.,c:They are driving more slowly than the normal traffic flow.
note: Typical signs of impaired driving include weaving between lanes, erratic speed changes, sudden braking, and other irregular driving behaviors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Passing is prohibited:
options: a:At intersections.,b:On hills and curves.,c:All of the above.
note: Passing is unsafe and illegal in places like hills, curves, intersections, and railroad crossings where you cannot see oncoming traffic clearly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before entering a roundabout, you must yield to which road users?
options: a:Bicyclists in the roundabout.,b:Pedestrians in the crosswalks at the roundabout.,c:Vehicles already in the roundabout.
note: Yield to vehicles already circulating in the roundabout; also be alert for and yield to pedestrians and bicyclists where they cross the roundabout approaches.

question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, what should you do?
options: a:Get out and walk for help immediately.,b:Lie down in the car and go to sleep.,c:Stay in your car and wait for help
note: If stranded in a snowstorm, remaining in your vehicle increases chances of being found and protects you from exposure; wait for help when possible.

question: Compared to daytime driving, driving at night is:
options: a:No more or less dangerous.,b:Less dangerous.,c:More dangerous.
note: Driving at night is more hazardous because visibility is reduced and glare and fatigue can impair driving performance.

question: Which parking scenario is allowed based on distance rules?
options: a:Parking within 10 feet of a fire hydrant.,b:Parking 25 feet away from a crosswalk.,c:Parking on a sidewalk.
note: You must not park within 20 feet of a crosswalk or within 15 feet of a fire hydrant; parking 25 feet from a crosswalk is permitted.

question: When is it permissible to cross a solid yellow center line?
options: a:To pass traffic moving in the same direction.,b:Only to make a turn into a driveway or side street.,c:At any time.
note: Solid yellow lines generally prohibit passing; you may cross them when making a turn into or out of a driveway, alley, or private road as allowed by law.

question: A driver who drives much slower than the posted speed limit is generally:
options: a:Potentially hazardous and may be required to pull over if causing a backup.,b:A very safe driver.,c:Always has the right-of-way.
note: Driving substantially below the normal flow of traffic can be dangerous; if you are impeding traffic on a two-lane road, you may be required to pull off and let others pass.

question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?
options: a:No passing zones.,b:School zones ahead.,c:Railroad crossings; yield to trains.
note: A crossbuck marks a railroad crossing; drivers must yield to approaching trains.

question: The single most effective thing to reduce your risk of injury in a crash is to:
options: a:Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.,b:Limit your driving to weekdays.,c:Wear your seat belt.
note: Wearing your seat belt is the most effective way to reduce injury or death in a collision.

question: A single dashed yellow centerline means:
options: a:Both lanes travel in the same direction.,b:Drivers may not pass.,c:Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
note: A single broken yellow line means traffic in both directions may pass when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a solid red arrow signal indicate?
options: a:It indicates a pedestrian crossing only.,b:The arrow means you may turn after yielding.,c:It has the same meaning as a circular red light — stop and do not turn in the arrow's direction.
note: A solid red arrow means the movement indicated is prohibited until the signal changes; treat it like a red light for that direction.

question: If a tire blows out while driving, what should you do first?
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly and gradually slow to a stop.,b:Slam on the brakes.,c:Keep driving normally until you find a service area.
note: Grip the wheel, stay in your lane, release the accelerator to slow, and only brake lightly once moving slowly to pull off safely.

question: When stopped by police for a violation or equipment check, what must a driver produce?
options: a:Only proof of insurance.,b:Only registration.,c:Driver's license, registration, and proof of insurance
note: Drivers must be able to present license, vehicle registration, and valid proof of insurance upon request.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when you get to an intersection showing a flashing red light?
options: a:Stop only if other cars are also approaching the intersection.,b:Stop only if other cars are already within the intersection.,c:Come to a full stop and go when it is safe to do so.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign: stop, yield the right-of-way, and proceed only when safe.

question: If someone has consumed alcohol, which will help them overcome its influence?
options: a:Only time,b:Hot coffee,c:Fresh air
note: None of these will sober a person; only the passage of time reduces the effects of alcohol.

question: Which devices are sometimes used to direct drivers into the correct turning lanes on highways?
options: a:Flashing red lights.,b:White lines on the side of the road only.,c:Arrow markings and lane-control arrows.
note: Arrows (on signs and pavement) guide drivers into appropriate lanes for turning or through movements.

question: What must you do if you are leaving your vehicle unattended?
options: a:Leave the engine running briefly while you run a quick errand.,b:Only set the parking brake.,c:Lock the ignition and remove the key from the vehicle.
note: When leaving a vehicle, stop the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake to help prevent theft or unintended movement.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must a driver do when approaching a flashing red traffic signal?
options: a:Slow down and continue without stopping.,b:Merge to the right.,c:Come to a complete stop
note: A flashing red signal has the same meaning as a stop sign: stop, yield, then go when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a solid yellow line next to your lane indicate?
options: a:You may pass with caution.,b:Do not pass from your direction.,c:Slow down.
note: A solid yellow line beside your lane means passing is prohibited from your direction.

question: Why should you avoid following other cars too closely?
options: a:You may not see the vehicle's turn signals.,b:You may not have time to stop if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly.,c:You may not see the road between the cars.
note: Following too closely reduces your ability to stop safely if the vehicle ahead suddenly slows or stops; maintain a safe following distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drive below the posted speed limit when:
options: a:You see a police car.,b:Entering a highway where there are other cars.,c:Anything makes conditions less than perfect.
note: Reduce your speed below the posted limit when road, weather, or visibility conditions make driving unsafe at the posted speed.

question: How should a properly adjusted lap belt fit?
options: a:Hidden beneath the seat so it does not show.,b:Loose for more comfort.,c:Buckled snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
note: Lap belts should fit snugly across the hip bones and lower abdomen; shoulder belts should rest comfortably across the chest.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must yield to other drivers when:
options: a:Your traffic signal is a green arrow.,b:When they are on a road to your left and you have reached an unmarked intersection at the same time.,c:When entering a street from a garage or alley.
note: Yield to traffic and pedestrians when entering the roadway from a driveway, alley, or garage; yield to the right at unmarked intersections when arriving simultaneously.

question: If your vehicle is blocking traffic after a collision, what is the correct action?
options: a:Move the vehicle off the traveled portion of the roadway if possible.,b:Never move the vehicle under any circumstances.,c:Wait for police before moving the vehicle.
note: After a minor crash, move your vehicle off the road if it's safe to do so, but remain at the scene to identify yourself and assist if needed.

question: How can you avoid being in a truck or bus driver's blind spot?
options: a:Flash your lights at the driver to make them look.,b:Avoid driving alongside them and do not tailgate.,c:Never pass them under any circumstances.
note: Large vehicles have significant blind spots to the sides and rear; avoid lingering alongside them and keep a safe following distance.

question: When stopped on an incline, you should allow a larger space cushion in front of your vehicle because:
options: a:The vehicle ahead may roll backward when traffic moves again.,b:It is required by law to stop farther back.,c:You should always leave extra room only at stop signs.
note: Allow extra space on uphill stops so if the car ahead rolls back you have room to avoid a collision.

question: Which of the following are important steps to drive safely at night?
options: a:Increase your following distance, ensure headlights are working, and avoid driving when tired.,b:Use high beam headlights at all times.,c:Drive faster to make the trip shorter.
note: Night driving reduces visibility; increase following distance, verify headlights are working, and avoid driving if you are fatigued.

question: At a railroad crossing marked only with a crossbuck (no lights or gates), what is the safe approach?
options: a:Always stop before crossing even if no train is coming.,b:Approach with extreme caution and cross only when you are sure no train is coming.,c:Speed across quickly to avoid stalling.
note: At crossings without active controls, look and listen carefully and only cross when the tracks are clear and you have enough room to fully clear them.

question: What does an arrow painted on the pavement typically mean?
options: a:Drivers in the lane may ignore the arrow without consequence.,b:Drivers in that lane must make the movement indicated by the arrow.,c:Drivers must come to a complete stop before using the arrow lane.
note: Pavement arrows indicate the mandatory movement(s) permitted or required from that lane; obey any accompanying signs or signals.

question: For drivers 21 and older in Idaho, what blood alcohol concentration (BAC) defines driving under the influence?
options: a:0.02 percent or higher.,b:0.04 percent or higher.,c:0.08 percent or higher.
note: In Idaho (and federally), a BAC of 0.08% or higher for drivers 21+ is the legal threshold for driving under the influence.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a two-lane road with opposite traffic, when should you return to the driving lane?
options: a:When there is enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.,b:Immediately after passing regardless of space.,c:Only when you intend to turn left.
note: Return to the right lane after passing only when you can see the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror and there is enough space.

question: If you are in another driver's blind spot, what is the safest move?
options: a:Stay in the blind spot and maintain speed.,b:Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.,c:Flash your lights constantly.
note: Do not remain in another vehicle’s blind spot; either speed up to pass or drop back so the other driver can see you in their mirrors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who may adjust speed limits in specific areas by posting speed limit signs?
options: a:Only the state government can post varying speed limits.,b:State and local authorities by posting speed limit signs.,c:No one; speed limits are the same everywhere.
note: State and local authorities may set and post speed limits for particular roads and conditions; obey the posted speed limits.

question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway, you should:
options: a:Sound your horn.,b:Check mirrors and signal.,c:Turn on your headlights.
note: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors, signal, and look over your shoulder to ensure the adjacent lane is clear; adjust speed as needed.

question: Where on the roadway are you most likely to encounter ice that freezes quickly in cold or wet weather?
options: a:On flat, open sections of road,b:Shaded areas such as those under trees or next to buildings.,c:On the sunny side of the road.
note: Sections of road shaded by trees or structures lose sunlight and warm more slowly, so they freeze before other areas and stay icy longer.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following statements about speed is correct?
options: a:Speeding always reduces crash risk.,b:Speeding is never dangerous if you are a skilled driver.,c:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
note: Traveling much slower than traffic can create hazards as other drivers may make risky passing maneuvers; speed contributes to crash severity.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which is permitted while stopped in a travel lane on the roadway?
options: a:Stop to drop off passengers.,b:Make a U-turn or back up if you missed your exit.,c:None of these — you should not stop in a travel lane.
note: You should keep moving in a travel lane until you can safely pull off the road; do not stop, back up, or make U-turns in a travel lane.

question: If a traffic signal shows a green arrow but the main light is red, what does that mean?
options: a:You must wait for a solid green light to proceed in any direction.,b:You may only drive straight ahead.,c:You may drive only in the direction the green arrow indicates.
note: A green arrow authorizes movement only in the arrow's direction, but you must still yield to any pedestrians and ensure the intersection is clear.

question: How can you avoid needing to make emergency stops in traffic?
options: a:Look ahead and maintain a safe following distance.,b:Honk frequently to make others aware of you.,c:Drive only in the right lane.
note: Maintaining a safe following distance and anticipating traffic conditions allows you to slow gradually rather than make sudden emergency stops.

question: If followed by a fire engine that is not using its emergency signals on a two-lane street, you should:
options: a:Continue to drive in a normal manner.,b:Speed up to get out of its way.,c:Stop as quickly as you can.
note: If an emergency vehicle is not using lights or siren, it is not responding to an emergency; continue driving normally.

question: What must you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights approaches?
options: a:Pull over to the side of the road and come to a complete stop when safe.,b:Try to reach your destination before it arrives.,c:Continue driving but avoid the emergency vehicle.
note: Yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles by pulling to the right edge and stopping when possible; if in an intersection, clear it then pull over.

question: What does a slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?
options: a:A reflective orange triangle.,b:A rectangular red sign.,c:A diamond-shaped yellow sign.
note: A slow-moving vehicle emblem is a bright reflective orange triangle indicating the vehicle normally travels 25 mph or less.

question: What must a driver do when pedestrians are in crosswalks marked by two solid white lines?
options: a:Proceed only if the pedestrian steps away.,b:Yield and give the right-of-way to those pedestrians.,c:Drive through because vehicles have the right-of-way.
note: Marked crosswalks indicate pedestrians have the right-of-way; drivers must stop and wait for them to clear the crossing.

question: On a two-lane road without bicycle lanes, what is the safest way to pass a bicyclist traveling in your direction?
options: a:Continue straight; the bicyclist should get out of the way.,b:Never pass until you reach a signal or stop sign.,c:Wait until no oncoming traffic is present
note: Pass bicyclists as you would any vehicle, giving them ample room (minimum 3 feet) and passing only when safe.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
options: a:Stop and wait for a green light.,b:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light warns you to slow down and proceed carefully, yielding to any vehicles or pedestrians in the intersection.

question: You must yield to emergency vehicles:
options: a:When you see a flashing red or blue light or hear a siren.,b:Only when other vehicles yield.,c:Under no circumstances.
note: Immediately yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles using audible or visual signals by pulling over and stopping.

question: When faced with an oncoming car on the left and a bicyclist on the right, what should you do?
options: a:Drive between them (split the difference).,b:Let the oncoming car pass,c:Pull onto the shoulder immediately.
note: Avoid confronting two hazards simultaneously; let the car pass first, then safely pass the bicyclist.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A red flashing traffic light is equivalent to which traffic control device?
options: a:A stop sign.,b:A solid red light.,c:A yield sign.
note: A flashing red light requires a full stop and then proceeding when it is safe, like a stop sign.

question: Drivers of motor vehicles must yield to a pedestrian under which conditions?
options: a:Only when the pedestrian is elderly,b:When the pedestrian is crossing or about to cross within a marked or unmarked crosswalk.,c:Only when driving at night.
note: Always yield to pedestrians who are crossing or about to cross in marked or unmarked crosswalks and be prepared to stop whenever pedestrians are present.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive simultaneously at an open (uncontrolled) intersection, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Either may proceed without yielding.,b:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.,c:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
note: At uncontrolled intersections, yield to the vehicle on your right if you arrive at the same time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another driver is trying to pass your vehicle, what is the correct action?
options: a:Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to allow safe passing.,b:Signal to the other driver when it is safe for them to pass.,c:Pull off the road.
note: When someone begins to pass on your left, check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed so the passing vehicle can return to the right lane safely.

question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, you should:
options: a:Maintain your current speed and steer straight.,b:Try to steer straight while gradually slowing by removing your foot from the gas pedal.,c:Brake hard immediately.
note: Hold the wheel firmly, keep the vehicle straight, ease off the gas to slow, and apply the brakes gently once you have control to pull off the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill with a curb, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Keep the front wheels straight and set the parking brake.,b:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.,c:Turn the front wheels away from the curb (to the left).
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your front wheels away from the curb so the vehicle will roll away from the street if the brakes fail.

question: What does a steady green arrow on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:You may proceed in the arrow's direction after yielding to vehicles/pedestrians already in the intersection.,b:It has no different meaning from a circular green.,c:You must stop and wait for a circular green.
note: A green arrow permits movement in the indicated direction; yield to traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection.

question: Which of the following can impair a person's ability to drive safely?
options: a:Only lack of sleep.,b:Alcohol,c:Only illegal drugs.
note: Driving ability can be impaired by alcohol, legal and illegal drugs, and fatigue. All these factors reduce safe driving performance.

question: What must you do when an emergency vehicle approaches using sirens and flashing lights?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way and follow loudspeaker instructions.,b:Ignore it if you are not in its lane.,c:Continue driving normally.
note: Yield to emergency vehicles using sirens and flashing lights, follow any loudspeaker instructions, and be aware they may travel in groups.

question: Many crashes are caused by which of the following behaviors?
options: a:Drivers traveling too fast for conditions.,b:Drivers consistently checking their mirrors and blind spots.,c:Drivers yielding the right-of-way.
note: Many collisions occur when a driver’s speed is too high for the road, weather, or traffic conditions; always adjust speed accordingly.

question: When changing lanes to the left, where should you glance to check your blind spot?
options: a:Over your right shoulder.,b:Over your left shoulder.,c:At your side mirror.
note: Check over the shoulder in the direction you intend to move to catch vehicles in your blind spot that mirrors cannot show.

question: If you are involved in an accident, what should you always do first?
options: a:Continue driving if the damage seems minor.,b:Leave the scene and report later.,c:Stop at or near the scene and remain safe
note: Stop and move to safety, remain at the scene, and avoid standing in traffic lanes; turn off ignitions of wrecked vehicles if safe.

question: When preparing to change lanes, what checks should you make?
options: a:Check only your side view mirror.,b:Quickly turn your head to check for other vehicles only.,c:Check your side view mirror and rearview mirror and glance over your shoulder.
note: Before shifting lanes, check your mirrors for approaching traffic and, just before you move, briefly glance over your shoulder to ensure the lane is clear.

question: To avoid driving unsafely because of health, you should:
options: a:Drive within your physical limitations.,b:Keep physically fit and have regular physical examinations.,c:Know the effect of any medicine on your driving ability.
note: Be aware of how medical conditions and medications affect your driving, and limit driving if your health could impair your ability to drive safely.

question: Pentagonal-shaped road signs are used to indicate what?
options: a:School zones or school crossings.,b:No passing zones.,c:Speed limits.
note: A pentagonal sign typically marks a school area or crosswalk; be alert for children and pedestrians nearby.

question: Which statement about drowsy driving is true?
options: a:Drinking coffee always makes a drowsy driver safe to continue.,b:Opening a window will keep you alert enough to drive safely.,c:Drowsy drivers can drive so poorly that they may appear to be intoxicated.
note: Drowsiness impairs driving similar to alcohol; measures like opening a window or coffee are insufficient to ensure safety — rest is required.

question: What are the colors of signs that indicate distances to upcoming highway exits?
options: a:Green with white letters,b:Yellow with black letters,c:Red with white letters
note: Guide signs indicating destinations and distances on highways are typically green with white letters or symbols.

question: If your vehicle hits an unattended parked car and you cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Must stay until the police arrive.,b:Leave a written notice with your name,c:Have done as much as you can.
note: If you strike an unattended vehicle, stop, attempt to locate the owner, and if you cannot, leave a written notice with your contact information and the circumstances of the accident.

question: If you have a green light but pedestrians are crossing against the signal, how should you proceed?
options: a:Speed up to pass before they reach your lane.,b:Honk and continue through the intersection.,c:Stop to allow the pedestrians to cross safely.
note: Even with a green light, yield to pedestrians who are in the crosswalk; wait until they have cleared the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a multilane highway, you should:
options: a:Watch for oncoming traffic.,b:Be sure the passing lane is clear.,c:Pass only on the right.
note: Make sure the lane you plan to use for passing is clear and signal your lane change before you move over.

question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic accidents?
options: a:Excessive speed under the driving conditions.,b:Following other vehicles too closely,c:Inattentive driving
note: Driving too fast for conditions is a major cause of crashes; inattention and following too closely are also frequent contributing factors.

question: Which combination provides the most effective protection in a crash?
options: a:Only an airbag.,b:Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.,c:Only a lap and shoulder belt.
note: Seat belts greatly reduce the risk of death or serious injury; airbags provide added protection in front-end crashes when used together with seat belts.

question: What typically causes hydroplaning?
options: a:Sudden turns only.,b:Stopping suddenly.,c:Driving too fast for wet conditions
note: At high speeds on wet roads, tires can lose contact with the pavement and ride on water, resulting in loss of traction (hydroplaning).

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you cross a single broken white or yellow line?
options: a:To pass or change lanes if it is safe and does not interfere with traffic.,b:Never under any circumstances.,c:Only to make a U-turn.
note: A single broken line indicates passing or lane changes are permitted when it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a roadway from a private road, you should:
options: a:Stop with part of your car on the roadway to alert other drivers.,b:Drive out fast to merge smoothly with the traffic.,c:Blow your horn to warn cars you are entering the roadway.
note: Yield to pedestrians and vehicles on the roadway when entering from a driveway or private road; do not force your way into traffic.

question: If your accelerator becomes stuck while driving, what is the correct immediate action?
options: a:Shift to park immediately.,b:Reach down and try to pull the accelerator up.,c:Shift the car into neutral and apply steady pressure to the brakes.
note: If the accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road, shift into neutral, brake steadily, then pull off the road and turn off the engine when safe.

question: Which of the following is a common effect of alcohol on driving?
options: a:It slows your reaction time.,b:It improves your coordination.,c:It increases your ability to judge distance.
note: Alcohol slows brain functions responsible for judgment, reaction, coordination, and distance estimation, impairing driving ability.

question: The most common color of warning signs is:
options: a:Yellow.,b:Green.,c:Red.
note: Most warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black symbols or text, indicating potential hazards ahead.

question: Increasing your vehicle's speed:
options: a:Increases your field of vision.,b:Decreases your field of vision.,c:Makes it easier to see cross traffic.
note: As speed increases, your field of vision narrows, reducing your ability to see hazards; slow down when necessary.

question: What is the primary safety benefit of wearing a seat belt?
options: a:Helps maintain control of the vehicle on winding roads.,b:Helps maintain control of the vehicle on rough roads.,c:Reduces the risk of injury or death in a crash.
note: Wearing a seat belt significantly increases your chances of avoiding serious injury or death in a collision and helps keep you positioned to control the vehicle.

question: A leaking exhaust system can:
options: a:Require your vehicle to have a tune-up sooner than normal.,b:Make you drowsy while driving.,c:Cause excessive oil use.
note: A leaking exhaust can let toxic fumes into the vehicle cabin, which may make the driver drowsy or unconscious; have exhaust repairs done promptly.

question: Car drivers should remember that large trucks:
options: a:Can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles.,b:Do not need more room to maneuver than passenger vehicles.,c:Have large blind spots.
note: Large trucks have significant blind spots and need more room to maneuver and stop; avoid lingering alongside them.

question: When you see a steady yellow arrow at a traffic signal, you should:
options: a:Should merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.,b:May turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,c:Should slow to a stop
note: A steady yellow arrow warns that a red arrow is about to appear. Stop if you can do so safely unless you are already in the intersection.

question: Anything that requires you to ___ could cause you to crash.
options: a:Only take your hands off the wheel.,b:Take your attention away from driving.,c:Take only your eyes off the road.
note: Distractions that take your eyes, hands, or attention away from driving increase the risk of a crash.

question: What are common effects of alcohol on driving ability?
options: a:Improved reaction time.,b:Increased alertness.,c:Loss of concentration
note: Even small amounts of alcohol impair vision, judgment, concentration, and coordination.

question: When driving near heavy trucks, other drivers should allow for:
options: a:Reduced noise levels from the truck.,b:Decreased stopping distance for large vehicles.,c:The increased stopping distance the truck requires.
note: Large vehicles need more stopping distance; remain visible to the truck driver and avoid lingering in blind spots.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering public traffic from a driveway or private road, what should you do regarding other drivers?
options: a:You may force your way into traffic.,b:Yield to drivers already on the public road.,c:You have the right-of-way.
note: Vehicles entering from driveways or private roads must yield to traffic already on the public road; merge only when it is safe.

question: Your vehicle's blind spot is the area:
options: a:You see in the rearview mirror.,b:You cannot see without turning your head.,c:Directly behind your vehicle only.
note: Blind spots are areas you can't see in mirrors and require a shoulder check to verify they are clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles arrive at an unmarked intersection simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle that honks first.,b:The vehicle approaching from the left.,c:The vehicle approaching from the right.
note: At intersections of similar roads without control devices, yield to vehicles coming from your right.

question: If you notice a vehicle defect that could affect safe operation, what should you do?
options: a:Correct the defect when you can afford it.,b:Correct the defect as soon as possible.,c:Drive the vehicle at slower speeds until you can fix it.
note: Any defect affecting safe operation should be repaired promptly before driving the vehicle whenever possible.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit.,b:Make a U-turn through the median.,c:Go to the next exit.
note: If you miss an exit, continue to the next exit and re-route; do not stop, back up, or make unsafe turns on the freeway.

question: Does the type of alcoholic beverage change how significantly alcohol affects your reflexes and judgment?
options: a:Beer impairs much less than wine.,b:No — any type of alcohol can impair reflexes and judgment depending on amount consumed.,c:Hard ciders and mixed drinks are always worse.
note: Impairment depends on the amount of alcohol in the bloodstream, not the beverage type.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you cross double solid yellow lines?
options: a:To turn left into or out of a driveway or to make a permitted left turn.,b:To pass a slower vehicle.,c:To change lanes at any time.
